explanation: Boxing converts the value type to object, unboxing retrieves it; the value is preserved.
String interning ensures compile-time string concatenation results in the same interned reference.
The null-coalescing operator ?? returns the right operand when the left is null.
Decimal type provides exact decimal arithmetic unlike double, avoiding floating-point precision issues.
Structs are value types; assignment creates a copy, so modifications to p2 don't affect p1.
Reference equality for boxed integers with small values uses cached instances per MSDN spec.
Char arithmetic uses ASCII values; subtracting '0' converts digit char to its numeric value.
Var infers array type from initializer; GetType().Name returns the element type with brackets.
NaN is not equal to itself per IEEE 754; use double.IsNaN() to test for NaN.
Null-conditional operator ?. returns null when receiver is null, then ?? substitutes 0.
